newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee gains v spot dlr, falls in forwards.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee gains v spot dlr, falls in forwards.

text.p: The Indian rupee ended up against the dollar in the spot market Monday but weakened sharply against the forward dollar, dealers said.
Forward premiums opened up after a long weekend and stayed firm but a sharp spurt in late afternoon caught leading market participants by surprise.
"One year forwards rose as much as 25 paise," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "And there were still payers."
Dealers said there was some corporate coverage on Monday but this alone could not explain the rise in premiums.
Dealer at two banks attributed the sharp rise to one year forward booking by a large petrochemical firm.
"Premiums jumped after 3.0 p.m.," said a corporate treasurer. "That shows today's movement is inter-bank rather than corporate-driven."
Dealers gave many plausible explanations but were at a loss to put a finger on what exactly triggered the jump in premiums.
"RBI official's comments at Goa about rupee's overvaluation led to expectations something was in offing," said a dealer.

A spurt in overnight call rates also changed the sentiment, dealers said. Call rates closed at 8.5-9.0 percent on Monday. As in the case of forward premiums, money market dealers were not able to pinpoint reason for the rise in overnight rates.
"The next inflows (into the banking system) are only in late September," said a dealer. "The cost of carrying a long dollar position works out to 0.25 to 1.0 rupee a day. Why do it?"
Redemption of FCNR(A) expatriate Indian deposits, leading to a shortage of rupees with banks, could be another reason prompting banks to pay premiums, a dealer said.
Aggregate FCNRA deposits are estimated at $1.5 billion.
The six month annualised premium closed at 5.54 percent compared to the previous close of 4.59 percent.

The spot rupee opened down at 35.72/73 compared to the previous close of 35.712/717 but the rupee began gaining as pipeline dollar supplies accumulated over the weekend started pouring in, dealers said.

The spot rupee closed Monday at 35.6975/7000 compared with 35.72/73 opening. The rupee breached the 35.70-barrier with deals at 35.6975 and a European bank said it sold dollars to RBI towards the end of the day at these levels.
"Even corporates are confused," said a dealer.
"They will wait and watch for the next few days before deciding their moves."
